summary: This note is a table of the National Football League's annual sacks leaders, listing for each season the player, his sack total, and his team. It runs from 1982 through 2017, with some seasons missing or listed under a shared year heading. Marked players, such as Doug Martin and Mark Gastineau, carry an asterisk that the note does not explain.
one_line: A table of NFL annual sacks leaders from 1982 to 2017, with each player's sack total and team.
key_facts: The note is a table of NFL annual sacks leaders listing year, player, sacks and team.
Doug Martin of the Minnesota Vikings recorded 11.5 sacks in 1982, the lowest total in the list.
Mark Gastineau of the New York Jets recorded 19.0 sacks in 1982 and 22.0 sacks in 1984.
Lawrence Taylor of the New York Giants recorded 20.5 sacks in the 1986 entry.
Reggie White of the Philadelphia Eagles appears twice in the list with 21.0 sacks and 18.0 sacks.
Michael Strahan of the New York Giants recorded 22.5 sacks, the highest total in the list.
Michael Strahan of the New York Giants also recorded 18.5 sacks in 2003.
J.J. Watt of the Houston Texans recorded 20.5 sacks in 2012 and 17.5 sacks in 2015.
Jared Allen recorded 15.5 sacks for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2007 and 22.0 sacks for the Minnesota Vikings in 2011.
Justin Houston of the Kansas City Chiefs recorded 22.0 sacks in 2014.
Vic Beasley of the Atlanta Falcons recorded 15.5 sacks in 2016.
Chandler Jones of the Arizona Cardinals recorded 17.0 sacks in 2017, the final entry in the list.
The note marks several players, including Doug Martin and Mark Gastineau, with an asterisk (*), but does not explain the mark.
